B73 check QC — cross-experiment donor content

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

June 26, 2026

Repo: sawers-rellan-labs/zealtiger

A B73 control must be a pure recurrent-parent rep — no introgression (≈ 0 donor genome-wide). This doc tracks every B73 rep across the three experiments (BrB-seq, SNP50K skim, MolBreeding target sequencing) — scored by each experiment’s caller, plus two count-HMM second callers: Skim-nilHMM on the same skim reads as Skim-RTI and BrB-nilHMM on the same BRB reads as BrB-RTI — and flags reps that are not actually clean B73 (localized donor on a chromosome → mislabel / contamination / real introgression). It exists because the BrB-seq B73 control PN1_SID15 turned out to be an impostor (a chromosome arm reads ~50% donor).

  • donor dosage = genome-wide donor-allele fraction (Σ len·state/2 / Σ len, state REF=0/HET=1/ALT=2); 0 = pure B73.
  • maxchr = the worst single-chromosome donor fraction — localizes an introgressed arm.
  • flag: clean (dosage < 0.02), borderline (0.02–0.10), impostor (> 0.10).
Code 
library(tidyverse); library(ggpubr)
pal <- c(REF = "gold", HET = "springgreen4", ALT = "purple4")

brbmap <- read_csv(params$brb_map, show_col_types = FALSE)
brb_b73 <- brbmap$name[grepl("^B73", brbmap$accession)]
calls <- bind_rows(
  read_csv(params$brb_calls,  show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(name %in% brb_b73) %>%
    mutate(exp = "BrB-RTI (r=7, wideseq)"),
  read_csv(params$skim_checks, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(donor == "B73") %>%
    mutate(exp = "Skim-RTI (r=5)"),
  read_csv(params$nilhmm_chk,  show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(donor == "B73") %>%
    mutate(exp = "Skim-nilHMM (counts)"),   # same skim reads as Skim-RTI, count-based caller
  read_csv(params$brbnil_chk,  show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(donor == "B73") %>%
    mutate(exp = "BrB-nilHMM (counts)"),    # same BRB reads as BrB-RTI, count-based caller
  read_csv(params$molb_calls,  show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(donor == "B73-bulk") %>%
    mutate(exp = "MolB-RTI (r=2)")
) %>% select(exp, name, chr, start_bp, end_bp, state)

qc <- calls %>% mutate(l = end_bp - start_bp + 1) %>%
  group_by(exp, name) %>%
  summarise(dosage = sum(l * state / 2) / sum(l),
            maxchr = max(tapply(l * state / 2, chr, sum) / tapply(l, chr, sum)),
            worst_chr = paste0("chr", names(which.max(tapply(l * state / 2, chr, sum) / tapply(l, chr, sum)))),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(flag = case_when(dosage > 0.10 ~ "impostor", dosage > 0.02 ~ "borderline", TRUE ~ "clean")) %>%
  arrange(desc(dosage))
cat(sprintf("B73 reps: %d (BrB-RTI %d, Skim-RTI %d, Skim-nilHMM %d, BrB-nilHMM %d, MolB %d) | clean %d | borderline %d | impostor %d\n",
            nrow(qc), sum(qc$exp == "BrB-RTI (r=7, wideseq)"), sum(qc$exp == "Skim-RTI (r=5)"),
            sum(qc$exp == "Skim-nilHMM (counts)"), sum(qc$exp == "BrB-nilHMM (counts)"),
            sum(qc$exp == "MolB-RTI (r=2)"),
            sum(qc$flag == "clean"), sum(qc$flag == "borderline"), sum(qc$flag == "impostor")))
B73 reps: 96 (BrB-RTI 35, Skim-RTI 12, Skim-nilHMM 12, BrB-nilHMM 35, MolB 2) | clean 78 | borderline 12 | impostor 6
Code 
cat(sprintf("BrB-nilHMM B73 control PN3_SID213 dosage = %.4f\n",
            qc$dosage[qc$exp == "BrB-nilHMM (counts)" & qc$name == "PN3_SID213"]))

Read: the impostor reps carry localized donor (high maxchr on one chromosome) — the signature of a real introgressed segment, not diffuse noise — so they are mislabeled / contaminated samples, not B73. The BrB-seq impostors cluster on plate PN1.

Chromosome painting — worst & clean B73 within each experiment

The 5 worst + 5 cleanest B73 reps within each caller — BrB-RTI, BrB-nilHMM, Skim-RTI, Skim-nilHMM, and MolB (only 2 reps, both clean) — ordered by donor content (ascending), caller labelled on the right. Shows BrB-seq carries both real impostors and clean reps, while Skim/MolB B73 are clean throughout. Each platform’s two callers (RTI + nilHMM) score the same reads. BrB-nilHMM is conservative — it under-calls donor and collapses ALT→HET on BRB (agent/nilhmm/BRB_run_findings.md), so its B73 reps read even cleaner than BrB-RTI’s; that makes it good at confirming a clean control but it will also under-flag a true impostor’s HET arm, so read BrB-RTI for impostor detection.

Code 
exps  <- c("BrB-RTI (r=7, wideseq)", "BrB-nilHMM (counts)", "Skim-RTI (r=5)",
           "Skim-nilHMM (counts)", "MolB-RTI (r=2)")
short <- function(e) case_when(grepl("BrB-nilHMM", e) ~ "BrB-nilHMM", grepl("BrB-RTI", e) ~ "BrB-seq",
                               grepl("Skim-nilHMM", e) ~ "Skim-nilHMM", grepl("Skim-RTI", e) ~ "Skim",
                               TRUE ~ "MolB")
# 5 worst + 5 cleanest within each experiment (MolB has only 2 reps -> both); order by donor dosage
# non-REF content = fraction of genome called HET or ALT (state > 0); the sort key
nonref <- calls %>% mutate(l = end_bp - start_bp + 1) %>% group_by(exp, name) %>%
  summarise(nonref = sum(l[state > 0]) / sum(l), .groups = "drop")
sel <- qc %>% filter(exp %in% exps) %>% group_by(exp) %>%
  filter(row_number(desc(dosage)) <= 5 | row_number(dosage) <= 5) %>% ungroup() %>%
  left_join(nonref, by = c("exp", "name")) %>%
  mutate(eo = match(exp, exps)) %>% arrange(eo, desc(nonref)) %>%   # cleanest (lowest non-REF) at TOP of each panel
  mutate(yidx = row_number(), ylab = sprintf("%s · %.3f", name, nonref),
         exp_lab = factor(short(exp), c("BrB-seq", "BrB-nilHMM", "Skim", "Skim-nilHMM", "MolB")))
paint <- calls %>% inner_join(sel %>% select(exp, name, yidx, exp_lab), by = c("exp", "name")) %>%
  mutate(state = factor(state, 0:2, c("REF", "HET", "ALT")),
         chr = factor(chr, levels = 1:10, labels = paste0("chr", 1:10)))

ggplot(paint, aes(xmin = start_bp/1e6, xmax = end_bp/1e6, ymin = yidx - 0.45, ymax = yidx + 0.45, fill = state)) +
  geom_rect() +
  facet_grid(exp_lab ~ chr, scales = "free", space = "free") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::unit_format(unit = "", scale = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = sel$yidx, labels = sel$ylab, expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  labs(title = "B73 reps — 5 worst + 5 cleanest within each experiment (ordered by donor content)",
       subtitle = "samples ordered by non-REF content (HET+ALT fraction) — cleanest at top | gold REF, green HET, purple ALT — a clean B73 is all gold",
       x = "Position (Mb)", fill = "Genotype") +
  ggpubr::theme_classic2(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
        strip.text.y.right = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold", size = 15),   # experiment label on the RIGHT, 90° CCW
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0.05, "lines"), panel.spacing.y = unit(0.4, "lines"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))

Recommended clean controls

Code 
qc %>% filter(flag == "clean") %>% group_by(exp) %>% slice_min(dosage, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(experiment = exp, sample = name, dosage = round(dosage, 4), maxchr = round(maxchr, 4)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Cleanest 3 B73 reps per experiment — use one of these as the control (NOT PN1_SID15).")

Use: for the BrB-RTI comparison docs, replace the PN1_SID15 control with the cleanest BrB-seq rep above. The impostor reps should be excluded from any B73-check pooling and flagged for the BRB-seq relabeling follow-up (docs/brbseq-sample-mislabeling.md).
